children: Novo Nordisk A/S (NVO, Financials), the Danish drugmaker behind Wegovy and Ozempic, is facing a problem that may arrive well before its patent cliff.
Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock to Sell after its latest survey suggested Eli Lilly could keep taking share in the fast-growing obesity and diabetes market.
Shares fell about 2% early Friday. The pressure is already showing up in prescriptions.

Morgan Stanley said growth in the Wegovy pill has slowed after a strong first half, while Lilly's Zepbound has captured much of the new Medicare demand created by the GLP-1 Bridge program. The competition could get tougher.
Lilly already has Zepbound and Mounjaro, while its Foundayo pill and experimental retatrutide could put more pressure on Novo Nordisk beginning in 2027. Then comes the longer-term issue.
Semaglutide is expected to generate about 75% of Novo Nordisk's sales in 2026 and could still represent 59% in 2031. Major patent expirations are expected in the early to mid-2030s.
That concentration leaves little room for execution mistakes.

For investors, the next test is whether Novo Nordisk can stabilize market share before patent pressure becomes the dominant concern. If Lilly keeps gaining ground now, the problem could become much harder to fix later.

title: Morgan Stanley Downgrades Novo Nordisk to Sell on Lilly Competition
